title: Sell Mineral Rights in Smithfield, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Smithfield, WV
metaDescription: Smithfield, Wetzel County mineral owners: core Marcellus farmland, multi-lease history, and family heir fractional interests.
heroLead: Smithfield is a small Wetzel County community sitting in ground that's part of the county's sustained core Marcellus development corridor.
intro: As with much of Wetzel County, the farmland around Smithfield has drawn consistent horizontal leasing interest over the past decade and a half, laid onto family tracts that in many cases have been held locally for generations.

sections.heading: Steady development in a core county
paragraphs: Smithfield's position within Wetzel County's broader core Marcellus acreage means surrounding tracts have generally seen earlier and more consistent leasing activity than counties further from the play's thickest section. Confirming whether your specific parcel is currently under lease, and on what terms, is worth checking directly rather than assuming based on the county's overall reputation.

sections.heading: Family tracts and multi-heir ownership
paragraphs: Ownership around Smithfield typically follows the pattern common throughout rural Wetzel County — farm tracts split among several heirs over multiple generations, each holding a sellable fractional share. A Wetzel County Courthouse records check in New Martinsville confirms your exact percentage.

sections.heading: What changes if your Smithfield tract enters a new unit
paragraphs: If an operator files a new pooling order bringing your Smithfield-area tract into a horizontal unit for the first time, your royalty calculation shifts from whatever a legacy well may have paid to a pro-rata share of the new unit's production. That's a meaningful change worth understanding before you sign anything the operator sends.
Reviewing the new pooling order against your existing lease terms, ideally before signing an amendment, protects your position going into the new unit.

faqs.question: Is Smithfield in an active part of Wetzel County?
faqs.answer: Yes, it sits within the county's broader core Marcellus acreage, though activity on any specific tract depends on individual lease status.

faqs.question: How many heirs typically share a Smithfield-area family tract?
faqs.answer: Multiple heirs sharing one original interest after several generations is common in this part of the county.

faqs.question: Where are the records for my Smithfield tract filed?
faqs.answer: At the Wetzel County Courthouse in New Martinsville.

faqs.question: What should I check before signing a new pooling amendment for my Smithfield tract?
faqs.answer: Compare the new pooling order's terms against your existing lease to understand exactly how your royalty calculation will change.

faqs.question: How do I locate the original severance deed for my Smithfield tract?
faqs.answer: Start with your current deed's referenced prior instrument, then work backward through the Wetzel County deed books until you reach the original mineral severance, noting any leases or partial assignments recorded along the way.
